title: The playoff game nobody scripted
story: In a do-or-die playoff game, our best pitchers weren't available, so I started a kid who hadn't had many pitching reps for us. It was a risk. He went out, threw strikes, and his pitches weren't fast and he didn't strike many kids out, but the slower speed meant fewer hard-hit balls, and the defense stepped up. That success started to feed the whole team: they hit well, ran the bases well and played an outstanding team game, because they had to. Everyone had to step up and play their part. That year they won the championship. The championship game ended on a dropped third strike with a runner on third and one out. The batter hadn't had a hit all year, not one. He'd been hit by pitches several times and was really scared at the plate. He ran, and the runner who scored from third was playing baseball for the first time. Those moments aren't scripted. They happen because kids are put in situations where they can fail or succeed.
